close_reason: Done. Error::Pem(DerError) and Error::Der(DerError) rustdoc now both explain the workspace's DerError naming rationale and cross-reference each other.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:219-222: the Error::Pem variant carries a DerError. This is because der::Error has an ErrorKind::Pem variant and the upstream load_pem_chain only returns der::Error.

The naming is consistent with pkix-revocation::CrlParseError(DerError), so renaming would diverge from the workspace pattern. But a future reader of the type definition sees:

  Error::Pem(DerError)  // wait, why is a PEM error a DerError?

The workspace-wide answer is "DerError is the opaque-newtype shape, used wherever any der::Error escapes a Tier-1 API surface, including PEM framing failures". That answer is in the rustdoc on DerError but not on Error::Pem itself.

Suggested rewrite (rustdoc only, no API change): add a single-sentence cross-reference on Error::Pem and Error::Der pointing at DerError::new's explanation of why this is one opaque type covering both PEM-framing and DER-body failures.

This is taste-with-engineering-basis: avoiding the "why does X wrap Y?" stall during a future code review of a similar new variant.
title: Error::Pem(DerError) is semantically odd: a 'PEM' error wrapping a DerError type name
